study.title: Hooks and Lines
study.question: How do I write lyrics and a melody that fit together?
study.passage:
Songwriting steps (written for this lesson):
1. Theme (5 minutes): Choose a theme you care about: a place, a friendship, a challenge, a season in Alberta, a goal.
2. Hook (10 minutes): Write a short line (3–7 words) that sums up the theme. Repeat it out loud. Does it stick?
3. Chorus (10 minutes): Four lines including the hook; rhyme scheme AABB or ABAB.
4. Verse (10 minutes): Four lines with details, images and story. Verses are more specific; the chorus is the big idea.
5. Fit words to rhythm: say each line, clap the syllables, and put stressed syllables on strong beats ("to-MOR-row" not "TO-mor-row").
6. Melody: sing the hook over a I–V–vi–IV progression, using chord tones on strong beats. The chorus melody is usually higher and more repetitive than the verse.
Content guide: school-appropriate lyrics; original words only.

study.title: Producer Mode
study.question: How do producers arrange a song in a DAW?
study.passage:
DAW workshop (written for this lesson; uses a free DAW such as BandLab in a browser or GarageBand on Apple devices):
1. Set up (5 minutes): new project, tempo (e.g. 90 BPM), key from your song, time signature 4/4.
2. Drums (10 minutes): add a drum track: kick on beats 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, hi-hat on eighths. Or use a drum loop that comes with the DAW.
3. Chords (10 minutes): MIDI keyboard or piano track playing your I–V–vi–IV progression, one chord per bar.
4. Bass (5 minutes): bass track playing the root of each chord.
5. Melody (5 minutes): play or enter your hook melody on a lead instrument.
6. Arrangement (10 minutes): plan sections on the timeline: intro (drums + chords), verse (lighter), chorus (all tracks, fuller), outro. Build contrast by adding and removing tracks.
Legal and responsible: use loops included with the DAW, your own sounds, or clearly licensed royalty-free or Creative Commons sounds with credit. Do not copy commercial recordings.

study.title: Record, Mix, Share
study.question: How do I record and mix a finished song?
study.passage:
Recording session (written for this lesson):
1. Set up (5 minutes): quiet space, headphones on (so the backing track isn't picked up by the microphone), microphone about a hand's width to 20 cm away.
2. Check levels: sing the loudest part; the meter should peak in the upper-middle, never red (clipping).
3. Record (15 minutes): record vocals or a live instrument over your arrangement. Record several takes and keep the best, or combine the best parts.
4. Mix (15 minutes): Levels: vocals or melody loudest, drums and bass steady, chords supporting. Panning: keep vocals, kick and bass centred; pan other parts slightly left or right. Effects: a little reverb gives space; too much sounds muddy. Listen on headphones and speakers.
5. Export (5 minutes): MP3 for sharing or WAV for best quality. Name: title_yourname.
6. Share in class and write a reflection: what you are proud of, one thing you'd change and what you learned about songwriting.
Privacy: share only in the class space; ask permission before sharing anyone else's voice.
